newsitem.title: USA: St Louis port navigation curbs remain - Coast Guard.
newsitem.headline: St Louis port navigation curbs remain - Coast Guard.

text.p: Navigation restrictions remained in place for the port of St. Louis on Tuesday due to high water on the Mississippi River there, a spokesman with the U.S. Coast Guard said.
"The safety zone was still in effect until the river at St Louis reaches less than 25 feet," said Lt. Drew Cheney, assistant chief of port operations, Coast Guard Marine Safety Office, St Louis.
He noted as of Tuesday morning, the Mississippi at St Louis was at 29 feet, up from Monday's 27.6 feet but one foot under flood stage of 30 feet.
The river was expected to crest at about 33 feet on Friday St. Louis, he said.
The Coast Guard imposed restrictions for the St. Louis area on Monday, setting up a safety zone from River Mile 184, north of St. Louis to River Mile 179, south of St. Louis.

Tows must have a minimum of 250 horsepower per 1,500 tonnes cargo, which is a standard loaded barge. Also, southbound tows greater than 600 feet excluding the tow boat may transit the zone during daylight hours only, Cheney said.
As water levels subside at the Twin Cities of Minneapolis and St Paul, Minn. restrictions were reduced.
On Monday, the upper Mississippi River at Minneapolis stood at 15.2 feet, below the 16-foot flood stage.
"The river has already crested there," Cheney said.
The river has been reopened to navigation from River Mile 857.6 (Minneapolis) to River Mile 615.1 (Guttenberg, Iowa), Cheney added.
But he said locks and dams from lower and upper St Anthony Falls, Minn. all the way down to Lock and Dam 13, near Fulton, Ill., remained closed.
"Lock and Dam 13 was shut down this Sunday due to high water," Cheney said.
"Tow boats cannot move because the locks are closed," Cheney said. However, small craft such as recreational and fishing boats, were allowed some movement between locks.

"Mariners should use the slowest, safest navigable speed and this is especially so for the upper Mississippi River to prevent possible wake damage to levees and other properties along the river," Cheney said.
Officials said water levels continued to rise in the Iowa, Illinois and Missouri areas along the river.
Lock and Dam 14, Pleasant Valley, Iowa and Lock and Dam 15, Rock Island, Ill., were expected to close on April 18.
Lock and Dam 16, Muscatine, Iowa and Lock and Dam 17, New Boston, Ill., were anticipated to close on April 16.
Also, Lock and Dam 18, at Gladstone, Ill, was expected to close on April 20 and Lock and Dam 20, Canton, Mo., on April 18. No plans were set for Lock and Dam 19 at Keokuk, Iowa, Cheney said.
"From Davenport, Iowa to St Louis, the levels are continuing to rise with the crest projected at Davenport by this Thursday," Cheney said.
"On Monday, Davenport was 17.36 feet, just two feet over flood stage."
((Doris Frankel 312-983-7305))
